crm_notes:
Summary: Lumen IDE Labs builds an in-IDE copilot used by developer teams (internal customers + external SaaS customers). Primary ask: dedicated capacity for predictable throughput during developer office hours (09:00-18:00 PT) with controlled burst to cover demos and heavy CI days.

Key requirements / constraints:
- Workload: real-time token streaming into editor (low token-latency critical).
- Target p50 token latency: <= 100ms for streamed tokens; p95 <= 250ms.
- Concurrency: baseline 500 interactive sessions, peak burst target 1,000.
- Determinism: model/version pinning required for reproducible completions across releases.
- Routing: prefer smart routing to cheaper variants off-hours; must support automatic fallback if primary capacity saturated.
- Cost sensitivity: developer-facing product with thin margins; wants clear committed-capacity pricing + burst-invoicing model.
- Security: VPC/private control plane, SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, audit logging, and EU data residency for some enterprise customers.

Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-05): "We need the latency to feel instant in the editor — anything >150ms and devs notice. Also need to pin models so our snippets don't drift between releases."

POC notes: 2-week POC agreed. SE to deliver test harness simulating editor streaming (see FF call ff_20260302_0193). Metrics to capture: token latency histogram, end-to-end completion time, tail latencies during bursts, cost per 1M tokens at configured batching.

Open items: procurement SLA request form, legal to confirm data residency control, SSO test account details.

Next steps (short): 1) Deliver dedicated POC environment + baseline perf report (Michael). 2) Pricing & contract draft (Ava). 3) Legal security pack (Priya) — SOC2 + KMS integration docs.

Staging hints/quick wins: recommend Optimize suggestions for batch-size + KV prefix caching to save costs while preserving latency; propose model quantization profile (13B quantized) for dev completions to hit latency targets.
